inputs.original_text: Folks, let’s talk about some genuine common sense and respect for the rule of law happening out in South Dakota this Thursday, courtesy of Governor Larry Rhoden signing Senate Bill 175 into law. It is just basic decency that anyone wanting to participate in our elections should have to prove they are actually United States citizens. This is about protecting the integrity of the ballot box, national sovereignty, and ensuring that our sacred civic duties are reserved for those who actually belong to our national family. Of course, the progressive elites and open-border ideologues are bound to cry foul, but this measure only applies to state elections and only impacts new registrants. It’s a modest, responsible step toward restoring order and accountability, and every state in the Union should follow South Dakota's lead in putting citizens first.
inputs.modified_text:
Look at what real leadership looks like. Governor Larry Rhoden just signed Senate Bill 175 into law this Thursday out in South Dakota, showing some backbone and genuine common sense by making sure anyone wanting to participate in our elections has to prove they are actually United States citizens. 

This is what happens when you stand up for national sovereignty, the rule of law, and the integrity of the ballot box instead of bending the knee to open-border ideologues and progressive elites. Voting is a sacred civic duty that belongs exclusively to our national family, not to just anybody wandering in. 

Of course, the left is crying foul, but let's be clear about what this actually is: a modest, responsible step toward restoring order and accountability that only applies to state elections and only impacts new registrants. Every single state in the Union needs to follow South Dakota's lead immediately and start putting citizens first.
